title: Vira Vovk
summary: Vira Ostapivna Selianska, known by her pen name Vira Vovk, was a prominent Ukrainian writer, critic, and translator, born on 2 January 1926 in Boryslav and passing away on 16 July 2022 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Her literary contributions and advocacy for Ukrainian culture have had a significant impact, particularly in the diaspora.

sections.heading: Early Life and Education
paragraphs: Vira Vovk was born in Boryslav in 1926 and spent her formative years in the Hutsul region, specifically in the town of Kuty, which was located on the Polish-Romanian border at that time.
She completed her secondary education in [[lviv|Lviv]] and Dresden, later pursuing studies in Germanics, music history, and comparative literature at the University of Tübingen.

sections.heading: Emigration and Academic Career
paragraphs: In 1945, Vovk emigrated with her mother to Portugal and subsequently moved to Brazil in 1949, where she settled in Rio de Janeiro.
She completed her university studies in Brazil and pursued postgraduate education at Columbia University in New York City and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München.
Vovk earned a PhD and became a professor of German literature at the Federal University of Rio de Janeiro.

sections.heading: Literary Contributions
paragraphs: Vira Vovk authored ten collections of poetry, ten novels, and eleven plays, and she was instrumental in translating works of Western writers into [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] and Ukrainian writers into Portuguese.
Her literary output has significantly contributed to the promotion of Ukrainian culture and language, particularly among Ukrainian communities abroad.

sections.heading: Awards and Recognition
paragraphs: Throughout her career, Vovk received several accolades, including the [[ivan-franko|Ivan Franko]] Literary award in 1957, 1979, 1982, and 1990, as well as the Blahovist award in 2000.
In 2008, she was honored with the [[shevchenko-national-prize|Shevchenko National Prize]], a prestigious Ukrainian state award recognizing her contributions to literature.

sections.heading: Legacy
paragraphs: Vira Vovk passed away on 16 July 2022 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, at the age of 96.
Her legacy continues to inspire future generations of writers and advocates for Ukrainian culture, particularly in the diaspora.
